title: Dive into Core AI model authoring and optimization (WWDC26 session 325)
gist: Apple's successor to Core ML. A model is converted to an asset that is specialised to the exact hardware and OS on first load, then cached. Developers can embed hand-written Metal kernels paired with reference functions, and Apple ships skills for coding assistants alongside.
changes: Fitting a model to the exact device becomes a platform default. The fitting is done by a vendor compiler; the kernels are still written by people.
caveats: Apple silicon only and opaque. No LLM tokens-per-second figures and no comparison with MLX or llama.cpp. The date is the conference month; the session page itself is undated.

bears_on.note: A platform now specialises each model to the exact hardware and OS on first load.

retired_why: Retired on 23 Nov to stay under eighty active signals. A vendor compiler fitting a model to one phone or laptop says nothing about fitting the stack to the load, and C2 has over thirty other supporting signals.
